newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives, dealers said on Thursday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. weekly jobless claims and January international trade data.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended March 15 are forecast to be around 316,000 compared with 307,000 reported in the previous week.
International trade for January is expected to show a deficit of US$10.7 billion against December's $10.29 billion.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning except for some position adjustments at the short end. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims and international trade figures," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact here," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday and weekend eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent, respectively. Week-fixed was unchanged from Thursday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2, six-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 percent.
